title: Dynamic quantum phase transitions in the two-leg Creutz ladder with long-range hopping
authors: J. A. da Silva, J. C. Xavier
abstract: In this work, we investigate quantum quenches in the two-leg Creutz model with long-range hopping, where the hopping amplitudes decay with distance as a power law characterized by an exponent $ν$ and have a finite range $D$. We first obtain the exact solution of a generic two-band model in momentum space. This allows us to compute the Loschmidt amplitude and, consequently, the dynamical free energy $f(\texttt{t})$ of the two-band model. We also show how to determine the Yang-Lee Fisher (YLF) zeros by solving a nonlinear equation. We demonstrate that the two-leg Creutz model in momentum space is a special case of the generic two-band model. Using these results, we identify the non-analyticities in the dynamical free energy $f(\texttt{t})$ at critical times $\texttt{t}_{c}$. We find that the number of nontrivial critical times $N_{s}$ depends on both $ν$ and $D$. In particular, we show that for small $ν$ and large $D$ the critical times become increasingly dense, leading, in the appropriate regime, to non-analyticities at an increasingly dense set of times---similar to what was observed by Xavier and Hoyos [Phys. Rev. B, $\textbf{108}$, 214303 (2023)] in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with long-range hopping terms.
summary:
This work theoretically investigates Dynamic Quantum Phase Transitions in the two-leg Creutz ladder with long-range hopping. By analyzing the dynamical free energy derived from an exact two-band model solution, the authors determine that the critical times are highly sensitive to the hopping decay exponent ($
u$) and the finite range ($D$). The findings suggest that for certain parameter regimes, the critical dynamics become extremely dense, indicating complex non-equilibrium behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates Dynamic Quantum Phase Transitions (DQPTs) that occur during quantum quenches in a specific lattice model.
main_result: The critical times where non-analyticities in the dynamical free energy appear depend on both the long-range hopping exponent (ν) and the finite range (D).
method: The analysis involves calculating the Loschmidt amplitude and the dynamical free energy from an exact solution of a generic two-band model in momentum space.
model_or_system: The system is the two-leg Creutz ladder incorporating long-range hopping, modeled as a spinless two-band free-fermion system. The Hamiltonian is analyzed under quantum quenches.
key_observables: Dynamical free energy f(t), Loschmidt amplitude Z(t), and the location of Yang-Lee-Fisher (YLF) zeros.
important_parameters: Long-range hopping exponent (ν), finite range (D), and quench parameters ($	heta, 	ilde{	heta}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on obtaining an exact solution for the generic two-band model in momentum space and identifying non-analyticities where YLF zeros hit the real-time axis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the parameter regions in which DQPTs occur for various values of D and show plots of the dynamical free energy f(t) near critical times.
paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the general theoretical framework by solving the two-band model, deriving expressions for $f(t)$ and YLF zeros. It then applies this framework to the Creutz ladder, analyzing how the critical times and the existence of DQPTs depend on the long-range hopping parameters $
u$ and $D$.
why_interesting: The connection between long-range interactions, quasi-periodicity, and the emergence of dense critical dynamics is a key topic in non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics, relevant to understanding thermalization and quantum chaos.
